item.content:encoded: Roberto Vannacci parteciperà sabato al forum di Cernobbio, ulteriore segnale della crescente attenzione che il leader di Futuro Nazionale sta attirando anche negli ambienti dell'economia e della finanza, mentre il suo partito continua a guadagnare consensi con un programma che ha suscitato forti critiche per le sue posizioni su migranti, donne e minoranze. Il forum TEHA, che si apre venerdì, è considerato uno degli appuntamenti più influenti del calendario italiano, riunendo ogni anno leader politici, manager, imprenditori e rappresentanti delle istituzioni internazionali per discutere i principali temi economici e geopolitici. Questo fine settimana arriveranno sul Lago di Como rappresentanti di sette governi, tra cui quello degli Stati Uniti, e alti funzionari dell'Unione europea. Vannacci, il cui partito, secondo i sondaggi, è quarta forza politica del Paese a soli sette mesi dalla sua fondazione, parteciperà sabato a un panel sul progetto europeo "tra integrazione e sovranità" insieme all'ex presidente del Consiglio Mario Monti, figura moderata e convintamente europeista. Decine di manager e imprenditori assisteranno al dibattito, che ha attirato più attenzione mediatica di qualsiasi altro evento in programma. Vannacci ha detto che potrebbe stupire la platea "con il buon senso". "Gli imprenditori italiani hanno bisogno che la politica smetta di sorprenderli ogni giorno con nuove tasse, adempimenti, costi, regole instabili e direttive europee," dice in un'intervista a Il Foglio pubblicata oggi. "A Cernobbio dirò con chiarezza che integrazione non può significare sottomissione e sovranità non significa isolamento". SFIDA PER RIELEZIONE DI MELONI Ex generale dell'esercito, Vannacci ha acquisito notorietà dopo la pubblicazione di un libro in cui denunciava "l'eccessiva visibilità" e i diritti concessi a minoranze e comunità LGBTQ, a suo giudizio una minaccia per le strutture sociali tradizionali. Tra le sue proposte figurano l'abolizione delle unioni civili per le coppie dello stesso sesso, l'espulsione degli immigrati che non si adeguano ai "valori della nostra civiltà" e il raddoppio, da 10 a 20 anni, del periodo di residenza legale necessario per ottenere la cittadinanza, oltre all'abolizione del reato di femminicidio e la difesa del patriarcato. In vista delle elezioni del prossimo anno, Vannacci rappresenta una sfida rilevante per la presidente del Consiglio Giorgia Meloni nel tentativo di mantenere il potere. Dopo l'uscita dalla Lega, che ne aveva sostenuto l'elezione al Parlamento europeo, Vannacci ha progressivamente sottratto consenso all'attuale maggioranza di governo. La sua presenza al forum ha suscitato proteste tra i partiti di opposizione. Carlo Calenda, leader di Azione, ha annunciato che boicotterà l'evento, accusando l'élite economica italiana di "inseguire l'ultimo populista di turno". Reuters ha contattato quattro importanti dirigenti d'azienda che parteciperanno al forum per chiedere un commento sulla presenza di Vannacci, ma tutti hanno rifiutato di esprimersi. Valerio De Molli, amministratore delegato del gruppo TEHA, ha affermato che il forum rappresenta una "piattaforma pensata per creare uno spazio di dialogo e confronto, anche tra persone che sostengono posizioni diverse". "UN UOMO PERICOLOSO" Vannacci non è il primo protagonista politico fuori dagli schemi a partecipare al forum di Cernobbio. Nel 2013 vi prese parte Gianroberto Casaleggio, principale stratega del Movimento 5 Stelle, quando il partito manteneva ancora un rapporto fortemente conflittuale con l'establishment economico italiano. Ex addetto militare a Mosca, Vannacci si oppone con forza all'invio di armi all'Ucraina ed è favorevole alla ripresa delle relazioni economiche con il Cremlino. Intervistato da La7, Calenda ha definito il leader di Futuro Nazionale "un uomo pericoloso" che agisce nell'interesse della Russia. Il panel con Vannacci e Monti rientra in una più ampia sessione dedicata all'Europa, che vedrà la partecipazione anche di Jordan Bardella, presidente del partito francese di estrema destra Rassemblement National, e sarà aperta ai giornalisti. Il senatore a vita ha dichiarato a Reuters di aver accettato l'invito senza alcuna esitazione e di aver esplicitamente chiesto che il dibattito fosse aperto al pubblico, a differenza della maggior parte degli incontri previsti dal forum. "Entrambi (Vannacci e Bardella) potrebbero un giorno ritrovarsi al governo. Il tema dell'impatto sull'Unione europea di una maggiore presenza di forze sovraniste-populiste è per me ineludibile, e utile per la comprensione collettiva", ha spiegato. "Ritengo importante sentire le loro posizioni anche in un contesto che non sia un comizio, ma nel quale possano essere sollevati punti critici".

item.title: Exportações ucranianas de grãos caem pela metade em agosto ante julho, diz sindicato
item.description: As exportações combinadas de grãos e oleaginosas da Ucrânia caíram para 1,2 milhão de toneladas métricas em agosto, ante 2,5 milhões de toneladas em julho, informou nesta quinta-feira o sindicato ucraniano de comerciantes UGA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As exportações combinadas de grãos e oleaginosas da Ucrânia caíram para 1,2 milhão de toneladas métricas em agosto, ante 2,5 milhões de toneladas em julho, informou nesta quinta-feira o sindicato ucraniano de comerciantes UGA. A UGA informou que o volume de agosto incluiu 649 mil toneladas de trigo, 211 mil toneladas de milho, 254 mil toneladas de canola, 66 mil toneladas de cevada e alguns outros grãos e oleaginosas. As exportações ucranianas de alimentos caíram drasticamente após os ataques russos aos portos ucranianos do Mar Negro. (Reportagem de Pavel Polityuk)

item.title: Suède-A dix jours du scrutin, les élections législatives s'annoncent serrées - sondage
item.description: La coalition de droite du Premier ministre suédois semble rattraper son retard sur l'opposition de centre-gauche avant les élections législatives du 13 septembre, selon un nouveau sondage publié jeudi.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La coalition de droite du Premier ministre suédois semble rattraper son retard sur l'opposition de centre-gauche avant les élections législatives du 13 septembre, selon un nouveau sondage publié jeudi. Alors que les précédentes études d'opinion faisaient état d'une victoire quasi certaine des sociaux-démocrates menés par Magdalena Andersson, les derniers sondages montrent que le gouvernement du Premier ministre Ulf Kristersson, en poste depuis 2022, garde ses chances de remporter le scrutin. La coalition de centre-gauche bénéficie de 50,6% d'intention de vote selon un sondage mené par Demoskop pour les quotidiens Aftonbladet et Svenska Dagbladet, alors que la coalition au pouvoir - qui comprend le parti anti-immigration les Démocrates de Suède - récolterait 47,3% des suffrages. L'écart de 3,3% est le deuxième plus petit observé dans les études d'opinion publiées cette année en Suède alors que la précédente étude d'opinion de Demoskop faisait état d'une différence de 5,8%. Selon le dernier sondage, le parti des Libéraux, partenaire de la coalition gouvernementale, ne récolterait que 2,8%, loin du seuil des 4% qui garanti un accès au Parlement. La droite serait alors créditée de 163 des 345 sièges parlementaires contre 186 pour la coalition de centre-gauche. Il y a deux semaines, la coalition de centre-gauche possédait [USN:L6N44F0HU TEXT:"une avance de 10 points"] dans un sondage mené par un autre institut, les observateurs indiquant à l'époque que le retard serait insurmontable avant le jour J. L'étude d'opinion de Demoskop a été menée auprès de 1.998 personnes entre le 25 août et le 1er septembre.

item.title: Mara sisters speak as one in Herzog's Venice contender
item.description: Sisters Rooney and Kate Mara said years of shared experiences helped them master a unique acting challenge: speaking in perfect unison for Werner Herzog's "Bucking Fastard", which premiered at the Venice Film Festival on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Kristian Brunse
item.content:encoded: Sisters Rooney and Kate Mara said years of shared experiences helped them master a unique acting challenge: speaking in perfect unison for Werner Herzog's "Bucking Fastard", which premiered at the Venice Film Festival on Thursday. In the film, inspired by real-life British twins, the Mara sisters play Jean and Joan Holbrooke, whose extraordinary closeness has them speaking in perfect synchrony, share the same dreams and fall in love with the same man. It is the first time the two have acted together on screen. "We had two weeks of rehearsal set up and me and Kate were together before that because we were quite nervous," Rooney Mara told Reuters. But Herzog said he was so impressed by what he saw that he cut the rehearsal period to just five days. "I said, 'No more. I'm completely confident it's going to be wonderful. Stop this, shut up, we'll meet in Ireland in front of my camera'," he told Reuters. "It's unprecedented what they are doing. We have not seen anything like this in film history, and I doubt that we will see anything like this in the foreseeable future again," he added. MUSICAL SYNCHRONISATION Rooney Mara, best known for her roles in "The Social Network" and "The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo," said all their time spent together gave the sisters an instant shorthand that clicked into place when the cameras rolled. "There was just an unspoken world between us that we didn't have to work very hard to create at all. I've never laughed so much, it was a very once-in-a-lifetime, unique experience." Kate Mara, whose credits include "House of Cards" and "24", said speaking in synchronisation "felt almost like a song". The film shows the two sisters falling in love with the same man, played by Orlando Bloom. When he ditches them for another woman, he has to take out a restraining order to protect himself from their fury. Bloom told Reuters it was uncanny acting alongside his co-stars. "They were almost like they were breathing together, dreaming together, loving together, thinking together," he said. "The movie feels like a poem, and they were the central focus that we were kind of marvelling at." Herzog is no stranger to Venice. The acclaimed German director, whose films include "Aguirre, the Wrath of God", "Fitzcarraldo" and "Grizzly Man", premiered "Scream of Stone" at the festival in 1991 and has returned several times since with both fiction films and documentaries. "Bucking Fastard" is one of 21 films competing for Venice's Golden Lion award, which will be presented on September 12.

item.title: In flood-ravaged Nepal valley nothing is left standing
item.description: From the air, the section of Nepal's Trishuli River valley, where rescuers are trying to reach hundreds of workers trapped in hydroelectric power plants, emerges as an utterly desolate grey expanse.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: From the air, the section of Nepal's Trishuli River valley, where rescuers are trying to reach hundreds of workers trapped in hydroelectric power plants, emerges as an utterly desolate grey expanse. Eight days since the [USN:L4N44V09R TEXT:"catastrophic flood"], the ground has either turned hard like concrete or has become a slippery wet mass, and no signs of any human settlement are visible across wide swathes. Arriving by helicopter, Reuters photographer Navesh Chitrakar saw excavators trying to move huge boulders from the mouth of a tunnel at Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower plant. But the opening was so small that Nepali rescue workers could only attempt to enter the tunnel by crawling inside. Authorities estimate that some 900 people are trapped inside six hydropower plants in the small Himalayan nation, where a glacier collapse last Wednesday sent a giant wave of mud, rock and water barreling through mountain valleys, killing over 1,200 people. Other workers at Upper Trishuli 3A were draining the water from inside the tunnel and preparing to conduct controlled blasts by drilling into the hulking boulders, so that the excavators could move in deeper. Villages like Syabrubesi, once a gateway for Himalayan treks dotted with houses, showed up as a layer of grey-coloured mud, with only a few buildings remaining. There were no visible signs of life in this apocalyptic setting, Chitrakar said, and marks on the looming mountains on both sides of the Trishuli river suggested that the flood waters may have climbed as much as 500 meters above normal levels. At the Gyirong border gate, where surveillance footage showed people attempting to flee seconds before a mudslide engulfed the crossing between China and Nepal, some rescue workers could be seen in red uniforms along with some heavy machinery. But there was nothing left standing, the Reuters photographer said. No buildings, no gate, no bridge.

item.title: Wall Street sube después de que Waller de la Fed dice que podría apoyar mantenimiento de tasas
item.description: Los principales índices de Wall Street abrieron al alza el jueves, después de que el gobernador de la Reserva Federal Christopher Waller dijera que podría apoyar mantener las tasas de interés sin cambios este mes si los datos confirman que las presiones sobre los precios se están moderando.
item.dc:creator: Niket Nishant, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Los principales índices de Wall Street abrieron al alza el jueves, después de que el gobernador de la Reserva Federal Christopher Waller dijera que podría apoyar mantener las tasas de interés sin cambios este mes si los datos confirman que las presiones sobre los precios se están moderando. * Estas declaraciones llevaron a los operadores a reducir sus apuestas a favor de un alza de tasas y podrían disipar el pesimismo en los mercados tras los últimos enfrentamientos militares entre Estados Unidos e Irán. * "Mi decisión sobre la orientación adecuada de la política monetaria se verá muy influida por lo que sepamos sobre la inflación de agosto", dijo Waller en unas declaraciones realizadas en un evento de Reuters NEXT Newsmaker celebrado en Washington. "Si se sigue avanzando hacia nuestro objetivo del 2%, estaré dispuesto a apoyar el mantenimiento de la tasa oficial en su nivel actual". * No obstante, señaló que podría ser necesario subir los costos de financiación si los datos de inflación muestran que persisten las presiones sobre los precios. Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, los operadores ven cerca de un 48% de probabilidades de que se produzca una subida este mes. * La volatilidad previa a las elecciones de mitad de mandato y la posible disminución de la liquidez en septiembre crean "un escenario en el que los inversores pueden reaccionar de forma exagerada y el mercado puede experimentar altibajos", señaló. * Un conflicto prolongado en Oriente Medio también podría complicar aún más las perspectivas de tasas, al agravar las presiones inflacionarias. Los futuros del crudo Brent subían un 0,49% en la sesión, su cuarto día consecutivo de ganancias. * El Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) subía 394,74 puntos, o un 0,74%, a 53.456,69 unidades; el índice S&P 500 (.SPX) sumaba 41,29 puntos, o un 0,54%, a 7.707,89 unidades; y el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) ganaba 160,2 puntos, o un 0,61%, a 26.378,03 unidades. * Broadcom (AVGO.O) caía un 5,26%, después de que sus previsiones de ingresos para el cuarto trimestre no alcanzaran las elevadas expectativas de Wall Street, lo que pone de relieve que las empresas que están en el centro de la expansión de la inteligencia artificial tienen un listón muy alto que superar.

item.title: Preços do café recuam no Vietnã em mercado calmo
item.description: Os preços do café robusta no Vietnã caíram ainda mais nesta semana devido a um mercado pouco animado, marcado por estoques baixos e demanda fraca após o longo feriado nacional do país, enquanto os prêmios do robusta indonésio subiram, informaram os comerciantes nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Phuong Nguyen, Mas Alina Arifin
item.content:encoded: Os preços do café robusta no Vietnã caíram ainda mais nesta semana devido a um mercado pouco animado, marcado por estoques baixos e demanda fraca após o longo feriado nacional do país, enquanto os prêmios do robusta indonésio subiram, informaram os comerciantes nesta quinta-feira. Os produtores do Planalto Central, o cinturão cafeeiro do Vietnã, venderam grãos a preços entre 91.200 e 92.000 dongs (US$3,50 a US$3,53) por kg, abaixo da faixa de 95.700 a 96.200 dongs registrada na semana passada. "As pessoas ainda não voltaram do feriado. O mercado está muito calmo agora", disse um corretor da região cafeeira. Os contratos futuros de café robusta para novembro fecharam em queda de US$14, a US$3.392 por tonelada métrica na quarta-feira. Outro ofereceu 89.500 dongs por kg para café a ser entregue em dezembro. "Embora o USDA tenha estimado que a produção na safra atual seria semelhante à anterior, muitos agricultores afirmaram que um grande número de cerejas verdes havia caído das árvores, gerando preocupações quanto à produção", disse o corretor. O Vietnã exportou 1,33 milhão de toneladas métricas de café nos primeiros oito meses de 2026, um aumento de 13,7% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior, segundo dados do governo. A receita com as exportações de café nesse período caiu 8,6%, para US$ 6 bilhões. Somente em agosto, o país exportou 132.000 toneladas, um aumento de 13,7% em relação ao ano anterior. Na Indonésia, os grãos de café robusta de Sumatra foram oferecidos com um prêmio de US$300 em relação ao contrato de novembro nesta semana, disse um trader, um aumento em relação ao prêmio de US$260 da semana passada para o mesmo período. Outro trader informou que os grãos foram oferecidos com um prêmio de US$200 em relação ao contrato de outubro, um aumento em relação ao prêmio de US$175 da semana passada para o período de setembro.

item.title: Israel liberará a cinco detenidos libaneses en el marco de las conversaciones con el Líbano
item.description: Israel liberará a cinco ciudadanos libaneses detenidos en el sur del Líbano tras comprobar que no tenían vínculos con grupos militantes, según informó el jueves la oficina del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israel liberará a cinco ciudadanos libaneses detenidos en el sur del Líbano tras comprobar que no tenían vínculos con grupos militantes, según informó el jueves la oficina del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu. Según la oficina, la decisión se tomó en el marco de las negociaciones con el Líbano para recuperar los restos mortales de los líderes de la comunidad judía secuestrados y asesinados allí a mediados de la década de 1980. Israel y el Líbano han llevado a cabo varias iniciativas en los últimos meses para localizar los restos, incluidas operaciones sobre el terreno, según la oficina de Netanyahu. Israel ya ha liberado a uno de los cinco, Malek Kamal Ghazi, que fue capturado en octubre de 2025 y entregado por la Cruz Roja a las autoridades libanesas en el paso fronterizo de Naqoura, según informaron a Reuters una fuente de seguridad libanesa y una fuente de la comisión de prisioneros. Las fuentes desmintieron las informaciones que apuntaban a que Ghazi era miembro de Hezbolá y afirmaron que los otros cuatro que iban a ser liberados también eran civiles. Señalaron que 35 detenidos libaneses permanecían en Israel, entre ellos 20 civiles. Israel y el Líbano firmaron en junio un acuerdo marco mediado por Estados Unidos que incluía el compromiso de trabajar por la liberación de los detenidos y la búsqueda y repatriación de los restos mortales. El acuerdo también prevé una retirada israelí eventual del sur del Líbano, a medida que el ejército libanés asuma el control y desarme a Hezbolá, grupo respaldado por Irán, condiciones que este último ha rechazado.

item.title: Índices sobem após diretor do Fed afirmar que pode defender manutenção dos juros
item.description: Os principais índices de Wall Street operavam em alta nesta quinta-feira depois que o diretor do Federal Reserve Christopher Waller afirmou que pode defender manutenção da taxa de juros neste mês caso os dados confirmem que as pressões sobre os preços estão diminuindo.
item.dc:creator: Niket Nishant, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Os principais índices de Wall Street operavam em alta nesta quinta-feira depois que o diretor do Federal Reserve Christopher Waller afirmou que pode defender manutenção da taxa de juros neste mês caso os dados confirmem que as pressões sobre os preços estão diminuindo. Os comentários levaram os operadores a reduzir as apostas em um aumento dos juros e podem dissipar o clima de pessimismo nos mercados após os recentes confrontos militares entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã. “Minha decisão sobre a postura adequada da política monetária será fortemente influenciada pelo que soubermos sobre a inflação de agosto”, disse Waller em um discurso preparado para ser proferido em um evento do Reuters NEXT Newsmaker em Washington. “Se houver progresso contínuo em direção à nossa meta de 2%, estarei disposto a defender a manutenção da taxa de juros no nível atual”, disse Waller. Mas os custos dos empréstimos podem precisar subir se os dados de inflação mostrarem que as pressões sobre os preços persistem, disse ele. Os operadores ainda esperam uma chance de quase 48% de alta nos juros neste mês, de acordo com a ferramenta CME FedWatch. A volatilidade antes das eleições de meio de mandato e a liquidez potencialmente mais escassa em setembro criam “um cenário em que os investidores podem reagir de forma exagerada e o mercado pode apresentar altos e baixos”, disse Kim Forrest, diretora de investimentos da Bokeh Capital Partners. Investidores ávidos por catalisadores positivos agora estão de olho nos dados de emprego nos EUA na sexta-feira, mas alguns alertaram para não se dar muita ênfase ao relatório já que o chair do Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, indicou que controlar a inflação continua sendo sua principal prioridade. Um conflito prolongado no Oriente Médio também poderia complicar ainda mais as perspectivas para os juros ao agravar as pressões inflacionárias. Os contratos futuros do petróleo Brent subiam 0,49% nesta quinta-feira, quarto dia consecutivo de ganhos. O Índice Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) subia 0,74%, para 53.456,69 pontos, enquanto o S&P 500 (.SPX) avançava 0,54%, a 7.707,89 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) tinha alta de 0,61%, para 26.378,03 pontos.

item.title: Número de militares iranianos que teriam sido mortos em ataques dos EUA nesta semana sobe para 13
item.description: A agência de notícias semioficial iraniana Tasnim informou nesta quinta-feira a morte de mais seis militares em ataques dos EUA nesta semana, elevando o número de mortos entre os militares para pelo menos 13.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A agência de notícias semioficial iraniana Tasnim informou nesta quinta-feira a morte de mais seis militares em ataques dos EUA nesta semana, elevando o número de mortos entre os militares para pelo menos 13. Os ataques dos EUA na terça-feira foram os mais intensos das últimas semanas. No relatório mais recente sobre as mortes de militares, a Tasnim informou que seis membros das Forças Armadas regulares, incluindo três pilotos, foram mortos no sul do Irã. A agência não forneceu detalhes adicionais sobre o local. A Tasnim havia informado anteriormente que os ataques de terça-feira haviam matado três membros da milícia paramilitar Basij na Ilha de Lavan, no Golfo, cujo funeral ocorreu no sul do Irã na quarta-feira. Os ataques também mataram quatro membros da Força Aeroespacial da Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica (IRGC) no oeste do Irã, de acordo com um comunicado da Guarda publicado na quarta-feira. As baixas militares iranianas no conflito que começou no final de fevereiro têm sido relatadas periodicamente, sem confirmação oficial do número total de vítimas. A guerra, que começou com ataques dos EUA e de Israel ao Irã, já deixou milhares de mortos, a grande maioria deles no Irã e no Líbano. Na quarta-feira, uma autoridade do Ministério da Saúde iraniano afirmou no X que, de 30 de agosto a 2 de setembro, 18 pessoas haviam sido mortas — incluindo quatro que participavam de um casamento — e 142 ficaram feridas, chamando novamente a atenção para o número de mortos entre a população civil. A Tasnim também informou que os ataques dos EUA ao sul do Irã no domingo, que ocorreram após um mês de trégua nos confrontos, mataram três pessoas. Duas delas foram identificadas como membros da Marinha do Corpo da Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica pela agência de notícias iraniana Nournews. Os EUA informaram que 18 militares foram mortos e mais de 750 ficaram feridos na guerra.

item.title: Forced labour: Will the EU’s threat of product bans succeed where supply-chain audits failed?
item.description: From December next year, companies face losing access to the European Union if their products are found to have been made with forced labour. The EU’s Forced Labour Regulation will provide belt and braces to its Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive, where companies in scope must identify, prevent, mitigate and account for adverse human rights and environmental impacts in their operations, subsidiaries and value chains.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Balch
item.content:encoded: From December next year, companies face losing access to the European Union if their products are found to have been made with forced labour. The EU’s Forced Labour Regulation will provide belt and braces to its Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive, where companies in scope must identify, prevent, mitigate and account for adverse human rights and environmental impacts in their operations, subsidiaries and value chains. While campaigners say effective enforcement of the forced labour regulation will require the European Commission and EU member states to significantly boost their investigative capacity, the prospect of product bans could be the stick that will encourage companies to carry out due diligence required under the CSDDD. What is clear is that voluntary due diligence approaches by companies have not succeeded in eliminating forced labour and other human rights abuses from global supply chains, despite the fact they have spawned a social auditing industry valued at $19.36 billion . Around the world, 27.6 million people are estimated to be the victims of forced labour , and 63% of them in the private economy. Human rights groups say wage theft, unsafe working conditions and harassment are widespread, with migrants and other vulnerable workers especially affected. Critics of the due diligence systems include suppliers, who complain of audit fatigue, and labour rights groups, who arguing that third-party assessments fail to capture the full picture , either because the audits are too superficial, too short, or because workers feel intimidated. A worker collects palm oil fruits at a plantation in Malaysia. Global human rights groups have repeatedly raised concerns over systemic labour abuses and poor working conditions across the sector. REUTERS/Bazuki Muhammad Neil Willings, global head of sustainability and supply chain at global compliance company SGS, insists that robust and diligent auditing offers companies a “solid baseline” about suppliers’ current performance as well as identifying areas for improvement. He also rejects a common assumption that supplier audits are laxer for being voluntary. He cites the 10-year-old Association of Professional Social Compliance Auditors (APSCA) as evidence of the sector’s robustness. Set up by the likes of Bureau Veritas, Intertek and SGS, the industry body now counts over 75 verified members, including most of the world’s major social audit providers. “There are still some pockets where industries choose to ignore bad practices. But looking back over the decades, a lot of progress has been made to improve supply chain compliance and reduce the risk of worker abuses,” he asserts. But Aruna Kashyap, associate director in the economic justice and rights division at campaign group Human Rights Watch, says most due diligence practices only look at one side of the story. “Companies are reluctant to look at the actual commercial drivers that often underpin labour abuses, like how contract prices are set or how fast orders have to be turned around. It’s as if social audits are almost set up to fail.” A new study , meanwhile, suggest that due diligence mechanisms are less important than the buyer-supplier relationships that sit above them. Clothing is displayed for sale in a GAP store. The brand found that its suppliers were more likely to comply with its specified social requirements when they were in a longer-term commercial relationship. REUTERS/Mike Segar Based on historic 2018 audit data from the U.S. fast fashion brand GAP, the study, in the Strategic Management Journal, found that suppliers were more likely to comply with social requirements specified by GAP when they were in longer-term commercial relationship with the brand. Suppliers that faced high competition within their product category also proved more amenable to changing their practices. Even more influential, however, is when there was a “threatened penalty” for failure to meet core labour standards: in this case, the loss of business. GAP’s initial policy was to work with low-performing suppliers to encourage them to improve, but it then introduced the threat of cutting commercial ties if suppliers failed to improve fast enough. The result was marked: an improvement by 0.8 standard deviations in supplier’s compliance scores and a 22-percentage-point fall in the probability of them failing their next audit. Without it, suppliers showed “no improvement” when they failed to meet GAP’s compliance requirements. The fashion giant’s policy today strikes the same balance, a company spokesperson confirmed. “Gap Inc is committed to supporting factory partners through remediation if we identify non-compliances, but in some instances violations of our code of vendor conduct can result in termination of commercial relations.” Matthew Amengual, an associate professor at Oxford University’s Saïd Business School and co-author of the paper, says the research provides at least three major takeaways. First, for voluntary approaches to work, buyers need to “show that they are serious”, by integrating corporate procurement and buying divisions into the compliance process. A worker sews garments inside a garment factory in Faridabad, India. REUTERS/Priyanshu Singh If the sole message from a purchasing department remains on quality and cost, they are unlikely to take on board injunctions from the compliance department about social rights. The second lesson is that relationships trump rules every time. If a supplier knows that a buyer won’t “cut and run”, either at the first hint of non-compliance or because of a lower-cost offer elsewhere, then the motivation to invest in social compliance measures is far higher, says Amengual. It’s a sentiment echoed by Arianna Rossi, senior research and policy coordinator at the International Labour Organization (ILO), who argues that a policing approach is less needed when buyers and suppliers know and trust one another. Buyers can foster such relationships not only through longer-term contracts or participation in joint labour accords, but also through financial or technical support for action plans put in place by suppliers to improve social standards. Rossi cites the example of ACT for Cambodia , a “supply-chain supported” initiative between trade unions, suppliers and purchasing brands to encourage collective bargaining agreements in the country’s fashion and footwear sector. “The kind of dialogue and opportunities to exchange ideas that a multistakeholder platform like this offers is really critical to helping brands hear the perspective of suppliers and workers, as well as to finding practical solutions to the problems behind instances of non-compliance,” she explains. Women work on the production line of a footwear factory in Cambodia. The ACT for Cambodia initiative encourages collective bargaining agreements in the country’s fashion and footwear sector. REUTERS/Ann Wang Importantly, such a strategy turns penalties into a signal of intent to external stakeholders, who might otherwise interpret a buyer’s willingness to collaborate as condoning poor practice in its supply chain. The third takeaway relates to the limitations of voluntary mechanisms, particularly when it comes to the power imbalance between suppliers and buyers. Corporations are not blind to this, with responsible buyers encouraging measures such as whistleblowing and confidential employee interviews to give more voice to workers. A case in point is EcoVadis’s Ulula service , which, among other functions, provides workers with a confidential channel to report abuses and seek remediation via their mobile phones. “Triangulating the information that suppliers provide with what workers provide is a good way to really get to the bottom of things and also to validate (audits, which) are a snapshot in time … What we can do here is something that happens much more continuously,” explains Antoine Heuty, founder of Ulula and senior vice-president of human rights at EcoVadis. Amengual also sees merit in toughening the transparency criteria of mandatory due diligence laws so they include consistent reporting on outcomes of mitigation efforts, such as how often contracts are cancelled due to non-compliance or whether remediation plans increase compliance, he says. At present, such data is almost impossible to obtain, Amengual states. Either companies don’t have the internal systems to offer an accurate picture, or, where they do have the data, they are reluctant to share it. As he notes: “No company wants to say, ‘Oh, we've gotten slightly better in our human rights violations’.”

item.title: AI cloud firm Nscale commits compute worth $3.5 billion for Figure's robotics ambitions
item.description: AI cloud firm Nscale on Thursday signed a multi-year deal to provide compute resources for the development of humanoid robotics company Figure's AI models and robots.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: AI cloud firm Nscale on Thursday signed a multi-year deal to provide compute resources for the development of humanoid robotics company Figure's AI models and robots. Nscale said it will initially commit $3.5 billion in compute resources for Figure. Here are some key details: Initial graphics processing units (GPUs) are targeted for deployment starting in the second half of 2027 in Barstow, Texas, Nscale said. The AI cloud firm, which competes with CoreWeave (CRWV.O) and Nebius (NBIS.O) , plans to scale the computing investment to more than $6 billion. Nscale said it will become a Figure shareholder and its preferred compute provider through the deal, powering the next generation of Figure's Helix models and humanoid robotics. The companies will also explore scaling Nscale's supply chain with humanoids. Nscale intends to potentially deploy up to 100,000 Nvidia (NVDA.O) chips for Figure.

item.title: Ex-Israeli NBA player's Swish Ventures raises $250 million for new VC Fund
item.description: Israel's Swish Ventures said on Thursday it has raised $250 million for its third venture capital fund, which it has now closed to new investors.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israel's Swish Ventures said on Thursday it has raised $250 million for its third venture capital fund, which it has now closed to new investors. Swish was founded in 2025 by Omri Casspi, the first Israeli to play in the National Basketball Association. He played between 2009 and 2019. Swish's assets under management have grown to $800 million. It has so far invested in 20 companies with a combined value of more than $60 billion. Eight of the companies are valued above $1 billion. The new fund aims to invest in 12 companies with an average of $20 million per company, either as co-lead investor alongside another fund or as a participating investor. It will focus on startups operating across cybersecurity, technology infrastructure, physical AI, defence, AI for industrial applications, and government technology. Investments are made in the Seed and Series A stages, enabling it to continue investing through growth stages. The fund's investors include existing Swish backers as well as new investors, including Sequoia Capital, U.S. institutional investors such as pension funds and American universities.

item.title: REUTERS NEXT Diretor do Fed Waller diz que taxa neutra pode ser mais alta, já que prêmio de segurança de Treasuries caiu
item.description: Não há mais prêmio embutido nos preços dos títulos do governo dos EUA considerados seguros e líquidos, afirmou o diretor do Federal Reserve Christopher Waller, em um evento da Reuters NEXT Newsmaker nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Não há mais prêmio embutido nos preços dos títulos do governo dos EUA considerados seguros e líquidos, afirmou o diretor do Federal Reserve Christopher Waller, em um evento da Reuters NEXT Newsmaker nesta quinta-feira. Waller afirmou que os rendimentos dos títulos -- inversamente proporcionais aos preços -- vêm subindo devido a preocupações com a situação fiscal, mas também por causa da competição por capital proveniente de investimentos em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial. Além disso, há evidências crescentes, segundo ele, de que o prêmio de segurança que impulsionava os preços dos Treasuries para cima e os rendimentos para baixo diminuiu. Ele disse que há muito tempo se preocupa com o fato de que “não há mais prêmio para títulos do governo dos EUA seguros e líquidos”. “E isso tem me levado a elevar minha estimativa da taxa neutra, o que implica taxas de juros de política monetária mais altas para qualquer taxa de inflação -- talvez você não esteja sendo tão restritivo quanto pensava”, acrescentou, em referência à política monetária do Fed.

item.title: Compradores asiáticos recorrem ao trigo australiano e argentino em meio a interrupções no Mar Negro
item.description: Importadores asiáticos de trigo adquiriram pelo menos meio milhão de toneladas métricas de trigo australiano e argentino em negócios recentes, segundo três fontes do setor, à medida que os compradores se apressam para substituir cargas do Mar Negro atrasadas por ataques a navios e à infraestrutura de exportação de grãos.
item.dc:creator: Naveen Thukral
item.content:encoded: Importadores asiáticos de trigo adquiriram pelo menos meio milhão de toneladas métricas de trigo australiano e argentino em negócios recentes, segundo três fontes do setor, à medida que os compradores se apressam para substituir cargas do Mar Negro atrasadas por ataques a navios e à infraestrutura de exportação de grãos. Os importadores da região, incluindo a Indonésia, o segundo maior comprador mundial de trigo, estão pagando preços significativamente mais altos por fontes alternativas de abastecimento, afirmaram as fontes, com vários países dependendo fortemente das importações para atender à demanda interna. "Houve negócios em grande volume na última semana a dez dias envolvendo trigo australiano e argentino para atender a necessidades urgentes", disse um trader baseado na Ásia, de uma empresa de comércio internacional que fornece trigo a moinhos da região. "Os importadores estão tentando obter remessas alternativas para cargas que não chegaram da Rússia e da Ucrânia." Os importadores globais de trigo enfrentam escassez de oferta, já que os ataques russos e ucranianos a portos e embarcações interromperam as operações nos terminais de grãos, forçando as transportadoras a adiar ou cancelar o carregamento de dezenas de cargas durante a alta temporada de exportação. O grupo norte-americano de commodities agrícolas ADM (ADM.N) informou nesta quarta-feira que um ataque com drone em 31 de agosto danificou seu terminal de grãos UEP no porto ucraniano de Odessa, no Mar Negro. Os compradores pagaram cerca de US$315 a US$330 por tonelada, incluindo custo e frete, pelo trigo branco premium australiano, enquanto os negócios com trigo argentino foram fechados por cerca de US$310 a US$315 por tonelada, segundo os operadores. Isso se compara à maioria das cargas do Mar Negro contratadas por cerca de US$260 a US$280 por tonelada para chegadas entre agosto e setembro. Os contratos futuros de referência de Chicago subiram cerca de 35% desde o final de junho, impulsionados em grande parte pela escassez de suprimentos do Mar Negro, enquanto os preços à vista dispararam entre os exportadores concorrentes -- Argentina, Austrália e Estados Unidos. O trigo em Chicago atingiu seu nível mais alto em três anos e meio na terça-feira, após relatos de que Moscou havia rejeitado uma moratória sobre os ataques na região do Mar Negro e lançado ataques noturnos contra a infraestrutura portuária ucraniana. Processadores de grãos na Ásia reservaram cerca de 2,0 milhões a 2,5 milhões de toneladas de trigo do Mar Negro para embarque entre julho e setembro, o que representa cerca de 30% a 50% da demanda de importação. No entanto, os crescentes atrasos nos embarques têm alimentado preocupações de que uma parte dos grãos possa não chegar aos compradores. Além da Indonésia, outros compradores asiáticos de trigo do Mar Negro incluem Bangladesh, Vietnã, Malásia, Tailândia e Sri Lanka. Embora os compradores estejam garantindo grandes volumes de trigo australiano e argentino, alguns recorreram a remessas em contêineres para atender às necessidades imediatas, afirmaram os operadores. "Algumas moageiras estão preferindo contêineres, pois combinaram com os fornecedores de adiar ainda mais a chegada das cargas do Mar Negro", disse um segundo trader com sede na Ásia. "Elas não querem se expor demais aos preços altos, então estão usando contêineres para atender às suas necessidades imediatas."

item.title: How the auto sector could be driving force in bid to scale plastic recycling
item.description: Every year, more than 800,000 metric tons of plastic from vehicles at the end of their lives are burned or sent to landfill in Europe. But this has to change, fast.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scott
item.content:encoded: Every year, more than 800,000 metric tons of plastic from vehicles at the end of their lives are burned or sent to landfill in Europe. But this has to change, fast. Under the EU’s proposed revision of its End-of-Life Vehicles Regulation (EU ELV), new vehicles will have to contain at least 15% recycled plastic within six years, rising to 25% within a decade, and at least a fifth of that material must have come from vehicles that have been scrapped. With around 10.8 million new passenger cars registered in the EU in 2025 (20% of which are not made in Europe) and 200–240 kg of plastic per vehicle, the 15% recycled content target implies the production of roughly 350,000 tons of recycled plastic annually. At the moment, no more than 2.5% of plastic from end-of-life vehicles finds its way into new cars, so there is a big gap. A new initiative to tackle this shortfall has emerged – not from carmakers but from a group of chemicals companies. The Global Impact Coalition (GIC), a platform focused on cutting carbon and introducing circularity into the chemicals sector, created a pilot project to show how a combination of mechanical and chemical recycling of plastic could help the automotive industry meet its targets. The project involved eight companies from the chemicals and waste industries and saw 100 end-of-life vehicles put through a process of dismantling, shredding and sorting to see if plastic components could be recovered from old cars and turned into material that is good enough to be used again. More than 800,000 metric tons annually of plastic from end-of-life vehicles are burned or scrapped. REUTERS/Jose Luis Gonzalez No single company in the automotive recycling chain has both the incentive and the capability to build this system unilaterally, so the entire value chain – from chemicals producers to carmakers to dismantlers and waste processors – needs to come together. “The raw materials exist but the system to convert them into automotive-grade feedstock doesn’t,” says Charlie Tan, CEO of the GIC. “There is a gap between regulatory ambition and how prepared the current system is to meet those goals.” The pilot proved that while it is technically feasible to recover and recycle plastics, there is still a long way to go on costs before a viable business case can be made. Nonetheless, says Tan, “the conversation is shifting from ‘can recycling automotive plastic work technologically’ to ‘can we build an economically viable supply chain and what would everyone’s role be?’”. Although the pilot project was led by the chemicals sector, it is carmakers that sit at the heart of circularity. “What makes the automotive sector unique is that it has one of the biggest volume feedstocks that can be collected for chemical recycling,” says Ana Sofia Almagro, global projects lead at the GIC. For plastics producers to scale up chemical recycling, they need long-term demand signals as well as a source of reliable, high-quality feedstock. Because of their need to use plastic recovered from old cars in new vehicles as a result of the new rules, automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) provide both. “There is an unusually close link between the supply of recycled plastic and the demand from OEMs for recycled plastic,” says Almagro. “That could provide the demand signal that chemicals companies need to build facilities for more chemical recycling.” The pilot project found that current sorting methods, and the make-up of many car parts, mean that the quality of recovered materials falls short of the requirements of today’s models. But with carmakers as both supplier and customer they can act to change that, says Dr Dirk Voeste, chief sustainability officer at Volkswagen. A Volkswagen employee works on a production line at the VW headquarters in Wolfsburg, Germany. REUTERS/Fabian Bimmer “We’re looking at being more circular by design, and what that means. How do we design the car of the future not just to reduce the amount of polymers that we use, but also to make it easier to disassemble? If we design a part differently, we can save so much time at disassembly,” says Voeste. Volkswagen is also working with the German government’s Open Hybrid Lab-Factory (OHLF), which is based in Wolfsburg, the company’s headquarters. OHLF’s research campus focuses on how to develop and produce materials that are resource-efficient, lightweight and circular. VW brand Audi, through its Material Loop project, is looking at ways to recycle not just plastics but also steel, aluminium and glass. There are well-established and successful recycling systems in place for these materials, but plastics are much harder to deal with. Plastics recycled mechanically are weaker than virgin plastic and can only be recycled a few times. There are also problems mixing different plastics, which melt at different temperatures, with contamination and the growing amount of packaging that uses composite or multi-layer materials, which are difficult to separate. “A key challenge for products that contain plastic is that they are very mixed together, and they have been bolted, welded or glued,” says Michael Puffer, head of alternative and new materials sourcing at chemicals producer Covestro. “It’s difficult to get material of a purity that it can be used as a feedstock for new products.” Recycling plastic chemically offers more flexibility because it reduces plastic waste to chemical building blocks, which can be used to create virgin plastic. But currently there is just 0.29 million tons of chemical recycling capacity operational in Europe, Almagro says, with a pipeline of planned projects with a capacity of 2.8 million tons. This compares to the 53 million tons of plastic waste produced in the EU in 2019, which is forecast to double by 2060, surpassing 100 million tons a year. “What is stopping more capacity being built is a lack of credible demand signals, which is almost as important as the price of the feedstock,” says Puffer. Bottles containing lithium hydroxide and nickel salts are displayed on a table at the battery recycling pilot plant in France. REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes Chemicals companies are keen to build more chemical recycling capacity because they are under pressure to cut their own emissions. Covestro, for example, is committed to becoming fully circular, and “climate neutral” by 2050. But collaboration and partnerships will be key to accelerating progress, Puffer says. “Circularity is a new business model,” says Voeste. “In the old days, we would design and produce a vehicle and then never see it again. Now, we want it back. We want spare parts, materials. It’s a completely different way of thinking than the old linear model. There are untapped revenue pools that we have not seen before.” These range from remanufactured parts to reduced raw material, resource and energy use. Other potential revenue streams include second-life batteries and as-a-service and subscription models. But carmakers are facing growing competition for low-carbon molecules, in particular from the shipping and aviation sectors. And the demand signals are not yet clear enough to scale up production, the goal of the next phase of GIC’s project. A whole new digital infrastructure will also be needed to allow all parts of the value chain to trace used plastic on its journey to becoming new products, and to allow carmakers to show they are complying with the regulations. “We need some kind of digital passport for cars,” says Voeste. “If you know everything about a car, it will be much cheaper and easier to disassemble.” The new ELV regulation introduces, among other things, a Circularity Vehicle Passport – a digital record of a vehicle’s materials, components and circularity data. Tan expects that there will be lessons for other sectors, ranging from shipping to fast-moving consumer goods and fashion. One area that Covestro has identified as very promising is mattresses. Some 44 million mattresses are disposed of every year in Europe, says Puffer, and they are full of polyurethane foam that can be repurposed. But when it comes to scaling up plastic recycling and making its production more circular, the automative sector is expected to be the driving force. item.title: Strong demand boosts US services sector activity in August
item.description: U.S. services sector activity picked up in August as strong demand lifted new orders to a 3-1/2-year high and drove input prices higher, suggesting inflation could remain elevated and compel the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates before the end of this year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. services sector activity picked up in August as strong demand lifted new orders to a 3-1/2-year high and drove input prices higher, suggesting inflation could remain elevated and compel the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates before the end of this year. The Institute for Supply Management said on Thursday its nonmanufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index advanced to 55.4 last month from 54.1 in July. A reading above 50 indicates growth in the services sector, which accounts for more than two-thirds of U.S. economic activity. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the PMI would climb to 54.2. The current PMI level is consistent with solid economic growth in the third quarter. The survey's measure of new orders received by services businesses surged to 60.9, the highest reading since February 2023, from 57.2 in July. The strength in orders aligns with robust domestic demand, which is partly being fueled by an artificial intelligence spending boom. With demand showing no signs of cooling, supply chains remained stretched last month. The survey's measure of supplier deliveries eased to 51.3 from 52.8 in July. A reading above 50 indicates slower deliveries. That measure has slowed for 21 straight months, pushing up input prices. Supplier delivery performance was initially impacted by tariffs on imports and most recently by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in its seventh month. The survey's measure of prices paid by businesses for inputs increased to 72.6 from 70.3 in July, suggesting inflation could stay above the U.S. central bank's 2% target for a while. Fed Chairman [USN:L6N44P0MM TEXT:"Kevin Warsh"] said last week the central bank will "have work to do" if policymakers don't get the confidence they need that inflation is falling to the 2% target. Financial markets are pricing in a roughly 64% chance that the Fed will raise its benchmark overnight interest rate by 25 basis points at its September 15-16 policy meeting, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. That rate is currently set in the 3.50%-3.75% range. Despite the surge in orders, services sector employment remained subdued last month. Economists say businesses are reluctant to add to headcounts because of policy uncertainty. The survey's employment sub-index was little changed at 47.8, suggesting a possible downside risk to nonfarm payrolls for August. A Reuters survey of economists expects the Labor Department on Friday to report that payrolls rebounded by 56,000 jobs last month after a [USN:L1N44U0SB TEXT:"surprise decline"] of 23,000 in July. That rebound would partly reflect a recovery in local government education payrolls. Some economists are, however, bracing for a second straight month of job losses after Temporary Protected Status for hundreds of [USN:L6N4431EV TEXT:"thousands of Haitians"] recently ended, impacting their work authorization.

item.title: Commerzbank to buy back own shares for €1.2 billion
item.description: Commerzbank , the German lender facing a takeover approach by UniCredit , said on Thursday it would launch a new share buyback programme of up to €1.2 billion ($1.39 billion) to boost the return for shareholders.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Commerzbank (CBKG.DE) , the German lender facing a takeover approach by UniCredit (CRDI.MI) , said on Thursday it would launch a new share buyback programme of up to €1.2 billion ($1.39 billion) to boost the return for shareholders. Commerzbank, valued at about €44 billion in total on the stock market, said the share buyback would begin Friday and run until February 10, 2027, at the latest. “With this next share buyback, we continue to consistently execute our attractive capital return policy,” said CEO Bettina Orlopp. The acquired shares will be cancelled, as was the case in two previous share buyback programmes, the lender added. Resistance by the bank and by the German government to a [USN:L6N44N0TQ TEXT:"takeover has weakened"] since the Italian lender in July reached a stake of nearly 50%, which is sufficient to sway shareholder resolutions, including naming board members. German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil plans to meet UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel, sources told Reuters last month, in the clearest sign yet that Berlin will engage directly with the Italian bank over the takeover attempt.

item.title: AbbVie's blood cancer therapy lowers disease progression, death risk in trial
item.description: AbbVie said on Thursday its therapy for a type of blood cancer has improved patients' response rate to treatment and reduced the risk of disease progression or death, meeting the main goals of a late-stage trial.
item.dc:creator: Puyaan Singh
item.content:encoded: AbbVie (ABBV.N) said on Thursday its therapy for a type of blood cancer has improved patients' response rate to treatment and reduced the risk of disease progression or death, meeting the main goals of a late-stage trial. As biosimilars chip away at sales of its arthritis treatment Humira, once its top-selling drug, the company is turning to acquisitions and other disease areas such as neuroscience and oncology to drive growth. The therapy, etentamig, showed an objective response rate of 74% in patients with refractory multiple myeloma, higher than the 45.7% recorded by standard treatments chosen by the trial investigator. ORR is the percentage of patients in a clinical trial whose cancer shrinks or disappears after treatment. Etentamig also increased survival without progression of the disease, and reduced the risk of the cancer worsening or death by 60% compared to other treatments in the 393-patient trial. "For AbbVie, the data add credibility to oncology but do not change the investment debate," said Citi analyst Geoffrey Meacham. Commercial execution for newer drugs Skyrizi and Rinvoq remains paramount, while investors are increasingly focused on "whether additional transactions can deepen AbbVie's 2030s growth profile." The trial included patients who received a median of three prior lines of treatment with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, a form of blood cancer that has returned after a period of remission or has stopped responding to treatment. After 12 months, 87.9% of patients receiving etentamig were still alive, compared to 72% of patients receiving standard treatments. Etentamig engages T-cells, which protect from infections and fight cancer, by targeting two proteins. Meachem said etentamig looks most differentiated as an additional post-CAR-T cell therapy, rather than a replacement for Johnson & Johnson's (JNJ.N) Carvykti or Gilead's (GILD.O) anito-cel. "CAR-T offers deep responses and a treatment holiday, while etentamig offers immediate availability, monthly administration and broader treatment-center access."

item.title: REUTERS NEXT Waller, de la Fed, pide paciencia para que se manifieste la desinflación
item.description: El gobernador de la Reserva Federal, Christopher Waller, dijo el jueves que, si los próximos datos confirman que las presiones inflacionistas se están moderando, se inclinaría por defender el mantenimiento de las tasas de interés sin cambios en la próxima reunión de política monetaria del banco central estadounidense.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby, Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: El gobernador de la Reserva Federal, Christopher Waller, dijo el jueves que, si los próximos datos confirman que las presiones inflacionistas se están moderando, se inclinaría por defender el mantenimiento de las tasas de interés sin cambios en la próxima reunión de política monetaria del banco central estadounidense. "Mi decisión sobre la orientación adecuada de la política monetaria dependerá en gran medida de lo que sepamos sobre la inflación de agosto", dijo Waller en un evento de Reuters NEXT Newsmaker celebrado en Washington. "Si se sigue avanzando hacia nuestro objetivo del 2 %, estaré dispuesto a apoyar el mantenimiento de la tasa de interés oficial en su nivel actual", agregó Waller. No obstante, advirtió de que también existe la posibilidad de una subida de las tasas de interés. "Si la inflación se dispara, consideraría una subida de tasas" en la reunión del 15 y 16 de septiembre, señaló. La tasa de interés de referencia actual de la Fed, entre el 3,50% y el 3,75%, "solo restringe ligeramente la demanda agregada", y "puede que no haga falta una gran aceleración de la inflación para que me decante por apoyar una política más restrictiva". Waller señaló que la inflación se sitúa "significativamente sobre" el objetivo del 2%, pero añadió que "se está avanzando de forma lenta pero constante hacia" ese objetivo. En declaraciones tras su comunicado oficial, Waller sostuvo que se inclina por mostrarse algo paciente con los datos que vayan surgiendo para confirmar que las presiones sobre los precios se están moderando. "Voy a parafrasear aquí a John Lennon: 'Démosle una oportunidad a la desinflación' y esperemos una reunión para ver cómo se presentan los datos", dijo Waller. "Hay que arriesgarse un poco para ver si la desinflación continúa. Pero no voy a arriesgarme demasiado", añadió.

item.title: Ibovespa avança com alívio em Treasury, sem tirar eleição do radar; CSN dispara
item.description: A bolsa paulista mantinha o fôlego positivo nesta quinta-feira, endossado pelo alívio nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro norte-americano, enquanto investidores seguem monitorando o fluxo de estrangeiros para as ações brasileiras e especulando sobre a disputa presidencial no Brasil.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: A bolsa paulista mantinha o fôlego positivo nesta quinta-feira, endossado pelo alívio nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro norte-americano, enquanto investidores seguem monitorando o fluxo de estrangeiros para as ações brasileiras e especulando sobre a disputa presidencial no Brasil. Na cena corporativa, CSN era o destaque com um salto de quase 20% na máxima após o grupo anunciar que Fabio Schvartsman será o novo presidente-executivo da companhia, substituindo Benjamin Steinbruch. Por volta de 11h25, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) , referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, subia 0,87%, a 186.810,75 pontos, caminhando para o 12º pregão com sinal positivo. Na máxima até o momento, alcançou 188.891,50 pontos. O volume financeiro somava R$9,48 bilhões. Nos Estados Unidos, o rendimento do Treasury de dez anos recuava a 4,76%, de 4,794% na véspera, após o diretor do Federal Reserve Christopher Waller afirmar nesta quinta-feira que está [USN:L6N44V0YL TEXT:"inclinado"] a manter os juros na próxima reunião de política monetária do banco central norte-americano. O índice S&P 500 (.SPX) , uma das referências do mercado acionário dos EUA, subia 0,5%, com investidores também analisando dados econômicos antes da divulgação de números sobre o mercado de trabalho norte-americano na sexta-feira, sem tirar a escalada da tensão no Oriente Médio do radar. No Brasil, agentes financeiros aguardam divulgação de pesquisa Datafolha sobre a corrida presidencial no país, conforme as eleições ocupam cada vez mais as atenções nas mesas de negociações. A trégua na saída de capital externo no final de agosto também alimenta expectativas de um retorno do fluxo estrangeiro para a bolsa paulista, que sustentou um avanço robusto do Ibovespa nos primeiros meses do ano. De acordo com analistas do Itaú BBA, o Ibovespa entrou em uma tendência de alta depois de muito tempo indefinido ou em baixa. "Esse cenário abre espaço para compras em ativos que superarem suas resistências e que acompanhem o índice na tendência de valorização", afirmaram no relatório Diário do Grafista. DESTAQUES CSN ON (CSNA3.SA) disparava 9,87%, após Fabio Schvartsman ser nomeado como o novo presidente-executivo da companhia, substituindo Benjamin Steinbruch, que assume a presidência do conselho de administração. De acordo com analistas, a mudança foi inesperada, mas representa uma notícia positiva, uma vez que atende a várias preocupações antigas dos investidores. Na máxima até o momento, saltou quase 20%. ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN avançava 1,86%, ampliando a recuperação após o desempenho negativo acumulado em agosto. No setor, BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) subia 1,84%, BRADESCO PN valorizava-se 0,56% e SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT mostrava elevação de 0,74%. BTG PACTUAL UNIT acompanhava os pares no Ibovespa com alta de 2,74%. PETROBRAS PN subia 1,1% e PETROBRAS ON (PETR3.SA) avançava 0,75%, endossadas pelo aumento dos preços do petróleo no mercado internacional. O barril sob o contrato Brent apurava [USN:L6N44V0ZE TEXT:"acréscimo"] de 0,67%, a US$96,26, após ataques entre EUA e Irã e novas ameaças de Israel contra Teerã reacenderem as preocupações com interrupções no fornecimento do Oriente Médio. VALE ON (VALE3.SA) recuava 1,58%, em meio a ajustes após forte valorização recente. Na China, o contrato futuro de [USN:L6N44V0UH TEXT:"minério de ferro"] mais negociado na Bolsa de Mercadorias de Dalian encerrou o pregão diurno com alta de 1,32%, com sinais de alívio nas restrições ao fornecimento de carvão de coque e uma retomada na atividade dos altos-fornos apontavam para uma melhora na demanda das siderúrgicas. PRIO ON (PRIO3.SA) caía 1,04%, tendo também como pano de fundo dados operacionais preliminares de agosto que mostraram queda na produção total da companhia para quase 186,1 mil barris de óleo equivalente por dia, de cerca de 196,3 mil barris em julho. No mês passado, a companhia vendeu 5,38 milhões de barris de óleo, ante quase 6,35 milhões em julho.

item.title: How NFL players are becoming game changers in the fashion industry
item.description: NFL players are remembered for what they do on the field, but what they wear off it has become just as highlight-reel-worthy in recent years, helping both the league and its players harness fashion as a tool to grow their brands.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Fernandes
item.content:encoded: NFL players are remembered for what they do on the field, but what they wear off it has become just as highlight-reel-worthy in recent years, helping both the league and its players harness fashion as a tool to grow their brands. A rising interest in athletes’ game-day outfits has helped the relationship between fashion and sports evolve into a world of opportunity. Nobody knows that better than Kyle Smith, the NFL’s fashion editor, whose job is not only to help players with their style but to teach them about the various ways they can immerse themselves in the fashion industry. “As I get to talk to our athletes, what I find is maybe they might not know about all the opportunities that exist for them,” Smith said. That includes starting clothing brands or walking shows at Paris Fashion Week, like Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow and Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson did in 2024. Fashion is also an approachable way to gain exposure among new and younger audiences. Social media plays a big role in generating interest as people consume content online, whether it is players’ game-day outfits or the league’s “Behind the Fit” video series that dives into the stories behind their style. Something as simple as a player wearing a band T-shirt could also help the league gain a new fan as it continues to grow globally, Smith said. “Then you’re following (that athlete) from team to team or their whole career, and you’re buying their jersey,” he said. “So it’s really important for the league to just find a new way to talk to a new audience, especially as we are growing internationally.” While fashion has opened new doors for the league and its athletes, it is also an avenue to tell stories. “There’s so many ways that our players are talked about, as the top wide receiver or top quarterback,” said Smith. “But I know our athletes have such rich backgrounds and interests and things beyond the field.” ATHLETES AS ASSETS Brands are also recognizing athletes as valuable assets to market products and reach different audiences. The league has official partnerships with Swiss luxury watchmaker Breitling and American retailer Abercrombie & Fitch. NFL players also walked the runway at February’s GQ Bowl, where Thom Browne presented his fall 2026 collection ahead of the Super Bowl. “Now brands are loving sending things over to players, contacting me or the players’ agents and (representatives) to make sure that the new collections are in their hands, because they can see that it adds a lot of value to the brand. That our players bring value through their own celebrity,” Smith said. “Players, they do what they want to do. And so there’s that authenticity that I think fashion is always begging for and yearning for, and our players bring that to everything that they do.” That authenticity is also helping them become game changers in the men’s fashion scene as they sport pieces that may not be considered traditionally masculine, such as when wide receiver JuJu Smith-Schuster wore a knee-length skirt to the Super Bowl in 2023. “If there’s something that they think is cool, they’ll wear it. They don’t really think about what is traditionally seen as men’s wear,” said Smith, adding that younger fans look up to players as style guides and trendsetters. “The fashion industry is shaping itself a little bit more around our athletes and the potential that our athletes have to shape fashion,” he said.

item.title: GoodRx offers health subscription for families, to launch as employee benefit in 2027
item.description: GoodRx, a prescription drug savings site, announced on Thursday a family healthcare subscription for access to common medical services and over 250 medications, and it plans to launch the program as part of employer health benefits in 2027.
item.dc:creator: Amina Niasse
item.content:encoded: GoodRx, a prescription drug savings site, announced on Thursday a family healthcare subscription for access to common medical services and over 250 medications, and it plans to launch the program as part of employer health benefits in 2027. The program, called Companion, offers 250 generic medications for free and discounted access to telehealth, vision, dental and lab services for families paying $24.99 each month. The subscription was previously only available directly to consumers on an individual basis. Individual Companion subscriptions cost $14.99 monthly. CEO Wendy Barnes said the launch is meant to address affordability gaps families are facing amid changes to health insurance coverage. "America’s healthcare affordability crisis is widening on both sides of the insurance divide," said Barnes, adding cost pressures are impacting entire households, while affordability tools often focus on individual patients. "Rising deductibles, out-of-pocket costs and coverage restrictions mean that having insurance no longer guarantees affordable access to care." GoodRx says it is already lining up employers that want to offer the program. Those partnerships are expected to start January 1, 2027. A spokesperson for GoodRx said employers can choose to subsidize the membership costs, and employees who choose to enroll would pay any remaining share. During this year's second quarter, GoodRx's subscription revenue increased 39% year over year, and uptake for the Companion program exceeded expectations, Barnes said. Employers expect healthcare costs to increase 9.2% in 2027, if they do not take action to mitigate expenses, according to the Business Group on Health. Some employers aiming to manage cost increases plan to offer plans with higher deductibles, requiring workers to pay more out of pocket before insurance coverage takes effect, the Business Group on Health said. "Pressure on insured consumers may be just as consequential as the number of people who lose coverage," said Barnes. "A person can have insurance and still face a prescription price they cannot afford."

item.title: Fed's Waller channels his inner John Lennon with a plea to 'give disinflation a chance'
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said that if upcoming data confirms inflation pressures are cooling off, he is inclined to argue in favor of keeping interest rates steady at the U.S. central bank's next policy meeting.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby, Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday that if upcoming data confirms inflation pressures are cooling off, he is inclined to argue in favor of keeping interest rates steady at the U.S. central bank's next policy meeting. "My decision on the appropriate stance of policy will be heavily influenced by what we learn about August inflation," Waller told a Reuters NEXT Newsmaker event in Washington. "If there is continued progress toward our 2% goal, then I am willing to support holding the policy rate at its current level," Waller said. But he warned that a path to higher interest rates is also in play. "If inflation comes in hot, I would consider a rate hike" at the September 15-16 meeting, Waller said. He noted that the current 3.50%-3.75% Fed policy rate is "only slightly restricting aggregate demand," and "it may not take much acceleration in inflation to nudge me into supporting tighter policy." Waller said inflation is "meaningfully above" the 2% target but added that it "is making slow but continued progress on reaching" that goal. In comments after his formal statement, Waller said he is inclined to be somewhat patient with the incoming data to confirm that price pressures are cooling. "I'm going to paraphrase John Lennon here. Give disinflation a chance," Waller said. When it comes to monetary policy and its stance versus inflation, "I'm not going to say let's wait until next year, but let's just wait and see if we get some improvement on this." INFLATION IS MAIN FOCUS Investors have been pricing in solid odds of a quarter-percentage-point rate hike at this month's Fed meeting. In recent weeks a [USN:L6N44O0TH TEXT:"wide range"] of central bank officials has signaled ongoing concern about inflation, with some calling for rate hikes and others signaling openness to action to bring what have been persistent above-target price pressure readings back to the target. Speaking last week at the Kansas City Fed's Jackson Hole economic symposium in Wyoming, Fed Chairman [USN:L6N44P0MM TEXT:"Kevin Warsh"] indicated that if inflation pressures did not moderate, action from the Fed to ensure they did was likely. After the release of Waller's remarks, stock market futures were little changed while traders trimmed bets on a rate hike at this month's meeting. They now see about even odds of such a move, down from about 60% earlier. Bond yields, which move inversely to prices, also fell on shifting monetary policy expectations. In his remarks on Thursday, Waller said his main policy focus at this time is on inflation, given the solid performance of the overall economy and the relative stability of the labor market. Waller said that some of the factors that have been driving up inflation recently are not likely to remain big price pressure drivers. "I don't see elevated energy prices and tariffs now as a significant source of ongoing inflation pressure," Waller said. The impact of the import tax increases has likely passed through the economy and higher energy prices tied to the war in the Middle East do not appear to be bleeding into other prices, he added. But he noted that he did see some upside risks to inflation. "Energy prices have moved up again and remain significantly higher than they were at the beginning of 2026, and the economy faces both pressure on technology goods prices related to the AI buildout and the possibility of more tariff increases."

item.title: Canada July trade surplus shrinks, US exports drop
item.description: Canada's trade surplus narrowed sharply in July as exports of energy and metal products shrank while imports rose, just weeks before Washington's new 50% tariffs begin to show up in statistics, posing a stiffer test for Canadian exporters.
item.dc:creator: Promit Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: Canada's trade surplus narrowed sharply in July as exports of energy and metal products shrank while imports rose, just weeks before Washington's [USN:L1N44I0GP TEXT:"new 50% tariffs"] begin to show up in statistics, posing a stiffer test for Canadian exporters. The trade surplus was C$769 million (US$557 million), compared with a four-year high surplus of C$4.2 billion posted a month ago, Statistics Canada said on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a surplus of C$3.57 billion in July. Exports dropped 2.3%, while imports increased 2.2%. Amid an escalating trade dispute with U.S. President Donald Trump's administration , Canada has been seeking to reduce its dependence on its neighbour and largest trading partner. The U.S. accounted for 66.35% of Canada's total exports in July, down from 69.39% in June and 72.64% a year ago. However, Canada's import dependence on the U.S. has only narrowed to 59% in the last 12 months compared with 62% in 2024. The July figures, Canada's fifth consecutive monthly trade surplus, extended a run of relatively resilient Canadian trade despite more than a year and a half of U.S. tariffs. However, Washington's latest duties, imposed last month, will provide a tougher test for exporters in the coming months. The decrease in exports in July was primarily led by energy products, which account for almost a quarter of Canada's total exports, and 95% of which usually flow south of the border. Their value dropped 4.4% in July, a third consecutive monthly decline after exports of crude oil decreased by 5.5%, with both prices and volumes falling, StatsCan said. Exports of metal and non-metallic mineral products, which posted an increase of 15.8% in the prior month, also shrank by 8.5% in July. As a result, Canada's total exports fell to C$76.14 billion, down from C$77.96 billion in June, but excluding metals and energy, exports increased 0.6% in July. The overall decrease in total exports in July was partially offset by higher exports of aircraft and other transportation equipment and parts, which surged by 34.9%. Imports rose in July to a value of C$75.37 billion, up from C$73.76 billion, StatsCan said, adding that it was the sixth consecutive monthly increase. This was led by an 11.4% increase in imports of motor vehicles and parts, mainly from the U.S. Exports to the U.S. dropped 6.6% in July while imports from the country increased by 1.8%, shrinking Canada's trade surplus with its main trading partner by more than 40% to C$5.9 billion. Stuart Bergman, chief economist at Export Development Canada, the country's official export credit agency, said that keeping the share of Canada's exports going to the U.S. below 70% was an encouraging trend. "Sheer gravity alone pulls exporters to the U.S. market," Bergman said, but added that there have been concerted efforts to shift some of that gravity to other markets, citing the increase in agricultural exports, especially canola to China and Japan. Year-to-date share of exports to the U.S. is around 68%, down from 73% in the year-ago period. Exports to countries other than the United States rose 7.4%, while imports increased 2.8%, leaving Canada with a non-U.S. trade deficit of C$5.1 billion, down from C$6.1 billion in the prior month. The Canadian dollar was trading firmer, up 0.35% to C$1.3792 against the U.S. dollar, or 72.51 U.S. cents.

item.title: Swedish election is a close race with 10 days to go, poll shows
item.description: Sweden's ruling right-wing bloc has narrowed the gap to the centre-left opposition ahead of a parliamentary election on September 13, according to an opinion poll released on Thursday, the second survey this week to indicate a close race.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sweden's ruling right-wing bloc has narrowed the gap to the centre-left opposition ahead of a parliamentary election on September 13, according to an opinion poll released on Thursday, the [USN:L8N44S1FM TEXT:"second survey"] this week to indicate a close race. While earlier polls have pointed to near-certain victory for the opposition headed by Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson, the latest surveys show that the government of Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, in office since 2022, may still win. Backing for the four centre-left parties was 50.6% in the Demoskop survey for dailies Aftonbladet and Svenska Dagbladet, while the three-party government and its support party, the anti-immigration Sweden Democrats, stood at 47.3%. "The election is in no way decided yet. It is going to be close," Andersson told reporters on Thursday. The gap of 3.3 percentage points between left and right was the second-smallest of any Swedish opinion poll published this year and compares with a 5.8 point gap in Demoskop's previous poll.
